RQ1.rationale: Directly presents a general/reusable CubeSat power-subsystem SysML model and modeling methodology.

RQ2.rationale: Claims reproducibility, time/cost/effort reduction, traceability, and requirement-status awareness from EPS MBSE artifacts.

RQ3.rationale: Implements pre-physical requirement/constraint checking from model data using Java-generated traceability tables.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: Explicitly extends INCOSE Space Systems Working Group CubeSat System Reference Model (CSRM) work; synthesis should treat it as a CSRM-family/open-source Papyrus extension rather than an independent flight-mission validation.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Address traceability in CubeSat MBSE, especially awareness of parameter impacts and whether requirements/constraints are met, using an open-source power-subsystem model and Java code.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_level_of_abstraction: PowerSubsystemCubeSat package with requirements, structure, behavior, and analysis. Structure includes generation, storage, supply/control, and bus; behavior is mostly nominal use-case/sequence level; analysis is a power budget via constraint blocks and parametric equations.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.deliberately_minimal_or_excluded: AD and SMD omitted; only nominal behavior shown; mission modes not discussed; model limited to power subsystem, with other subsystems future work.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: Method uses generic CubeSat standard requirements, mission-specific requirements, assumed external parameters, and known power-budget equations. Limited behavioral knowledge is handled by showing only nominal behavior and allowing future extension to modes/other diagrams.
key_evidence_quotes: This model-based approach for CubeSat subsystems helps to visualize and understand what is needed for the design of a CubeSat power subsystem, while guaranteeing that the designers are clearly aware of which requirements are being met and which are not.
For our model, an assumptions profile was created and applied in order to include assumptions.
The model can be found in the project repository.

eps_verification_specific.eps_requirements_represented_and_links: Requirements are divided into general CubeSat standard requirements and mission-specific requirements; requirement constraints are extracted and evaluated by Java. claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text: A Papyrus SysML power-subsystem model plus Java extraction code enables parameter-impact traceability and automatic requirement/constraint verification for CubeSat EPS design scenarios.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: In the demonstration scenario, calculated values match expected power-budget results and the output flags 0<PSAM as respected and Batt*1.2<BC as not respected.

key_findings_by_rq.RQ1: A CubeSat EPS can be represented in a compact SysML/Papyrus package organized into requirements, structure, behavior, and analysis; behavior can be limited to nominal use cases/sequences and extended later to mission modes.
key_findings_by_rq.RQ2: Supported outcomes are strongest for traceability/reproducibility and weak for cost/time/effort reduction. The open-source model and repository support reproducibility claims, while the Java example supports requirement-status awareness.
key_findings_by_rq.RQ3: Pre-physical verification is implemented as model-derived parametric/requirement checks: Java reads the .uml model, applies assumptions and constraints, and outputs respected/not-respected flags for design scenarios.
